gallery.credit: Photograph taken by chris_j_wood on the 28th May 2003, with original filename DCP_1011.jpg. Originally from en.wikipedia; description page is/was here.
gallery.description:
San Francisco Maritime Museum of the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park in Aquatic Park.
The buildings in the background are pejoratively known as San Francisco's Buck Teeth, and their building (which cut off many maritime views) led to San Francisco's passage of building height limits, in the interest of view preservation.

gallery.description:
Looking back on  the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park from along the shore.
Hyde Street Pier is the site of the San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park a National Park. The park has been here for years and offers the sights, sounds, smells and stories of Pacific Coast maritime history. It is free and you only pay if you want to go aboard the ships.

gallery.description: Crowley's in the lower left. View includes ROCHAMBEAU (built 1902; bark, 3m), WILLIAM P.
